items.headline: Bitcoin ETFs post their biggest daily outflow since June
items.blurb: US spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $485M on Oct 7, led by IBIT, FBTC and ARKB, wiping out October's early inflows; another outflow followed on Oct 8.
items.why_matters: This week's slide was driven by institutional selling rather than leverage — demand has to return before the $83–87k range can be reclaimed.

items.headline: Bitcoin rebounds to $82k after Trump rules out Iran strikes
items.blurb: Selling ran out near $80.3k late Thursday; BTC recovered to about $82k after Trump said the US would not strike Iran before the Nov 3 midterms, easing oil fears.
items.why_matters: Analysts flag ~$81k as support and ~$83.3k / $85.5k as levels to reclaim; a break below ~$80.3k raises downside risk.

items.headline: Oil near $100 and 30-year yields at a 2002 high weigh on risk
items.blurb: Daily ship attacks around the Strait of Hormuz kept Brent near $100 and pushed the 30-year Treasury yield to about 5.7% midweek, while most Fed officials still expect another hike this year.
items.why_matters: Macro is the main headwind for crypto right now; September CPI on Oct 14 and the Oct 27–28 FOMC are the next swing events.

items.headline: Ether ETFs extend their outflow streak; SOL funds also see redemptions
items.blurb: Ether ETFs shed about $161M on Oct 7, a seventh straight losing session, and solana ETFs also saw outflows as selling broadened across crypto funds.
items.why_matters: Institutional demand for altcoins is weak — a soft spot for a SOL-heavy model.
